requirements.text: The streak is decoration only: it never intercepts pointer input, never changes the button's accessible name, role or state, never adds a focusable element, and never shifts layout.

Every new option is documented for library consumers: a first example in README.md, entries in the API reference, a recipe in the examples, a description in the features page, and an additive note in breaking-changes, with the existing previous/next links kept.

Existing buttons and the existing chevron mount streak are protected: characterization tests record today's split-button layout, mount streak and focus ring before the production change, and buttons that do not opt in keep their current markup, classes and behaviour.

The effect stays cheap at scale: enabling it on many buttons adds no per-button timers, observers, event listeners or retained subscriptions, adds no runtime dependency, and stops all work when the sweep ends.
Keep the release version metadata and its tests in step. The additive release needs one version everywhere, so the package files and the tests that read them must agree.
Automated guard for the decoration-only contract. The streak must never make a button harder to click, read or lay out, so the guarantee needs a test rather than a review note.
Automated guard for the many-button cost. A decoration must not turn into hundreds of timers, listeners or observers on a screen full of buttons.
The streak is decoration only: it never intercepts pointer input, never changes the button's accessible name, role or state, never adds a focusable element, and never shifts layout.
tests: R10: clicking a button during its sweep runs the action exactly once
R10: keyboard activation during a sweep still runs the action once
A2: every focus and programmatic layer is click-through and absolutely inset
A2: an opted-in button has the same accessible name, role, state and disabled value
R10: a toggle and a busy button keep their state values while the streak plays
R10: opting in adds no DOM element, no aria-live announcement and no focusable node
R10: the split wrapper stays out of the tab order and is not announced
R10: at high zoom the band stays inside the button and adds no scrollbar
A2: the sheen rules contain no size, spacing or font declarations

requirements.text: Every new option is documented for library consumers: a first example in README.md, entries in the API reference, a recipe in the examples, a description in the features page, and an additive note in breaking-changes, with the existing previous/next links kept.
tests: R11: the README shows a first focusSheen example and a sheenTrigger example

requirements.text: Existing buttons and the existing chevron mount streak are protected: characterization tests record today's split-button layout, mount streak and focus ring before the production change, and buttons that do not opt in keep their current markup, classes and behaviour.
tests: A1: package.json and both root package-lock entries read 1.9.0
A1: breaking-changes has the matching additive 1.9.0 section
A1: the stale toggle release assertion no longer pins the old version
R12: no existing public export is removed or renamed
R12: the only public addition is the optional ZestCustomProps fields

R12: the split wrapper only gains relative positioning and the overlay radius when the sheen is in use
R12: toggle-mode buttons behave exactly as before when the sheen is not used
R12: busy buttons and dropdown items behave exactly as before when the sheen is not used
A3: a plain regular button keeps its current wrapper element, classes and DOM
A3: a split wrapper and its two segments keep their current classes and gain no sheen classes
A3: the existing focus-ring rule is still the focus indicator
A3: the existing chevron mount-streak rule and keyframes are unchanged
A3: a button that does not opt in keeps its click behaviour and adds no extra elements
R6: a split button that does not use the sheen keeps its one-time chevron mount streak
R6: a regular button has no chevron mount streak to suppress and gains no sheen class
R8: the API page documents every ToggleOptions prop and the README shows a toggle example

requirements.text: The effect stays cheap at scale: enabling it on many buttons adds no per-button timers, observers, event listeners or retained subscriptions, adds no runtime dependency, and stops all work when the sweep ends.
tests: R13: a hundred opted-in regular buttons schedule no timers and add no listeners
A3: opting in adds no listener to a mixed screen of a hundred regular and split buttons
A3: opting in adds no ResizeObserver to regular buttons and no extra observer to split buttons
R13: the existing split-button width measurement is unchanged and left behind on unmount
R13: a button unmounted during a sweep leaves nothing scheduled
R13: rapid programmatic triggers on many buttons build no backlog
R13/A3: the sweep runs once with fill both and adds no runtime dependency
